title: Normalized proper/open interchange commutes with projection
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and consider a commutative square of schemes
$$\begin{array}{ccc}A&\xrightarrow{k}&B\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ C&\xrightarrow{i}&D\end{array}$$
with $k,i$ quasi-compact open immersions and $r,p$ proper. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, and put $P_h=Lh^*$ and $R_h=Rh_*$. Put $B_C=B\times_D C$, with projections $b:B_C\to B$, $q:B_C\to C$, and $s=(k,r):A\to B_C$. Use the clopen immersion $s$ and projection $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$ that is identity on $s(A)$ and zero on the complementary open. Let
$$\alpha:P_pi_!\xrightarrow{\beta}b_!P_q\xrightarrow{b_!\pi_sP_q}b_!s_!s^{-1}P_q\cong k_!P_r$$
and let $\gamma:i_!R_r\to R_pk_!$ be its proper-adjunction mate, with precisely the normalization of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Let $\pi_h$ be the counit-defined projection maps of [def-exchange-projection] and $\delta_i,\delta_k$ the canonical open tensor isomorphisms of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. For every derived object $M$ on $A$ and $N$ on $D$,
$$\gamma_{M\otimes^L P_rP_iN}\,i_!(\pi_{r;M,P_iN})\,\delta_i
=R_p(\delta_k)\,\pi_{p;k_!M,N}\,(\gamma_M\otimes 1).$$
Both sides go from $i_!R_rM\otimes^L N$ to $R_pk_!(M\otimes^L P_rP_iN)$, using the canonical pullback identifications. The identity is natural and requires no Tor or boundedness condition on $M,N$.
The same identity holds as an equality before evaluation in the unbounded derived categories of strict semilinear coefficient systems $((A_{E,n})_T)_n$ on the pro-etale sites, with exact system pullbacks, derived system direct images, termwise open extensions, system tensor and the intrinsic system comparison $\Gamma_Q$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. In that version $\alpha$ is the same clopen-projection composite on the ringed diagram sites and $\gamma=\Gamma_Q$. It is an equality of system maps, not a conclusion from their evaluated equalities.

proof.text: Use [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] for the geometry of the square: $s=(k,r):A\to B_C$ is clopen, $bs=k$, $qs=r$, and $\alpha$ is exactly the specified base-change map followed by projection onto $s(A)$. This geometric assertion has no hypothesis on an input complex. Write $J=i_!$, $K=k_!$, $E=R_rM$, $X=P_iN$, $Y=P_pN$, and $T=P_rX=P_kY$. All tensors below are derived; canonical pullback/tensor identifications are understood. For an open $j$ write $\delta_j(U,V):j_!U\otimes V\to j_!(U\otimes P_jV)$. The normalizations in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] make these maps and the open base-change map identities after restriction and the open units.

proof.text: First check the tensor square for the base-change factor $\beta:P_pJ\to b_!P_q$. For arbitrary $H$ on $C$, its two routes have source $P_p(JH\otimes N)$ and target $b_!(P_qH\otimes P_bY)$: one applies $P_p\delta_i$, then $\beta_{H\otimes X}$ and the pullback tensor comparison; the other applies $\mu_p$, then $\beta_H\otimes1_Y$ and $\delta_b$. Both source and target lie in the image of $b_!$: use $\beta_H$ and the open tensor isomorphism to identify the source with $b_!(P_qH\otimes P_bY)$. Thus full faithfulness of $b_!$ reduces equality to restriction by $P_b$. Under the open units, $P_b\beta$ and $P_i\delta_i$ are identities. The remaining maps on both routes are the canonical pullback/tensor comparison on $P_qH\otimes P_bY$, using $P_bP_p=P_qP_i$. Hence the square commutes. Here the comparison is the canonical one for the commutative ringed pullback square, as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence].

proof.text:
The clopen-projection factor also respects tensor: in $B_C=s(A)\amalg(B_C\setminus s(A))$, $\pi_s$ acts by $(1,0)$. Tensoring it with $P_bY$ still acts by $(1,0)$ on the two components. The open tensor comparison for $s$ restricts to the identity on $s(A)$; on the complementary component its target is zero. Consequently projection before tensor and projection after tensor agree, followed by $\delta_s$. This is an identity of the given termwise clopen projections on complexes and hence of their derived classes, using the canonical tensor comparisons. The comparisons for the composite open $bs=k$ agree with $\delta_k$: both are maps between objects in the image of $k_!$, and after restriction to $k$ they are identities, so full faithfulness gives equality. Combining this calculation with Step 2 gives, for every $H$ on $C$, the explicit identity
$$K(\mu_r)\,\alpha_{H\otimes X}\,P_p(\delta_i)=\delta_k\,(\alpha_H\otimes1_Y)\,\mu_p.$$
Both sides run from $P_p(JH\otimes N)$ to $K(P_rH\otimes T)$.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); agent tensor/counit calculation with the normalized ringed-site maps

proof.text:
Put $Z=M\otimes T$ and $a_r=(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1_T)\mu_r:P_r(E\otimes X)\to Z$. The counit definition of $\pi_r$ gives $\varepsilon_{r,Z}P_r(\pi_r)=a_r$. The mate definition of $\gamma$ gives $\varepsilon_{p,KW}P_p(\gamma_W)=K(\varepsilon_{r,W})\alpha_{R_rW}$ for every $W$. Therefore the transpose under $P_p\dashv R_p$ of the left side of the claimed identity is
$$K(\varepsilon_{r,Z})\,\alpha_{R_rZ}\,P_pJ(\pi_r)\,P_p\delta_i
=K(\varepsilon_{r,Z}P_r\pi_r)\,\alpha_{E\otimes X}\,P_p\delta_i
=K(a_r)\,\alpha_{E\otimes X}\,P_p\delta_i.$$
The middle equality is naturality of $\alpha$ for the arrow $\pi_r:E\otimes X\to R_rZ$.

proof.text:
Transpose the right side under the same adjunction. Naturality of $\varepsilon_p$ first moves $R_p\delta_k$ out of the transpose; the defining adjunct equation of $\pi_p$ then gives
$$\delta_k\,(\varepsilon_{p,KM}\otimes1_Y)\,\mu_p\,P_p(\gamma_M\otimes1_N).$$
Naturality of $\mu_p$ replaces this by
$$\delta_k\,((\varepsilon_{p,KM}P_p\gamma_M)\otimes1_Y)\,\mu_p
=\delta_k\,((K\varepsilon_{r,M}\,\alpha_E)\otimes1_Y)\,\mu_p.$$
Now apply naturality of $\delta_k$ to $\varepsilon_{r,M}:P_rE\to M$, and then the identity of Step 3 with $H=E$. The result is
$$K(\varepsilon_{r,M}\otimes1_T)\,K(\mu_r)\,\alpha_{E\otimes X}\,P_p\delta_i
=K(a_r)\,\alpha_{E\otimes X}\,P_p\delta_i,$$
which is the transpose computed in Step 4. The adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so the original maps agree. All substitutions are natural in $M,N$.

proof.text: These calculations use arbitrary inputs in the unbounded ringed-site derived categories. In particular [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] supplies the counit-defined map for arbitrary sheaves of commutative rings and all objects, so the use of its formula does not specialize the finite ring $\Lambda$ to a quotient DVR or impose invertibility of its order. [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] also has no boundedness or Tor hypothesis. We never invert $\pi_p$, $\pi_r$ or $\gamma$, nor invoke a proper projection formula or proper base-change isomorphism on these inputs. This proves precisely the finite constant-coefficient identity claimed.

proof.text: We identify the stipulated system $\Gamma_Q$ intrinsically, rather than from its finite evaluations. Let $\widetilde\gamma$ be the proper-adjunction mate of the clopen $\alpha$. The realization node characterizes $\Gamma_Q$ by $\lambda_QP_i\Gamma_Q=1$ under the open unit, where $\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\cong S_r$ is obtained by open restriction, $k=bs$, $J_s=S_s$ for the clopen $s$, and direct-image composition. Make exactly those identifications in $P_i\widetilde\gamma$. Mate pasting identifies the restricted unit/counit maps with the unit/counit of $P_r\dashv S_r$; the restricted open base-change map is the identity by open normalization, and the clopen projection acts as identity on $J_sM$. Thus the composite $\lambda_QP_i\widetilde\gamma$ is $S_r\varepsilon_r\circ\eta_rS_r=1_{S_r}$ by the triangle identity. Since $J_i\dashv P_i$ gives a bijection on the relevant Hom sets, its adjunct characterization implies $\widetilde\gamma=\Gamma_Q$. This argument uses only the intrinsic open-restriction characterization and canonical composite adjunctions, and is independent of the total-limit comparisons or the finite evaluated arrows.

proof.text: For the system assertion, apply Steps 1--5 inside the unbounded derived module categories of the ringed diagram sites themselves. [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison] supplies the exact system inverse images and their derived adjunctions on these unbounded categories. [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] explicitly supplies the same open-unit, tensor and base-change normalization on the diagram topoi. The operations and intrinsic $\Gamma_Q$ are the simultaneous ringed-diagram constructions stipulated in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]; Step 7 identifies $\Gamma_Q$ with the proper mate of the same clopen-projection $\alpha$. Thus the system analogue of the mate equation in Step 4 is an equation in the system category. On system complexes the clopen projection in Step 3 is literally identity on the open component and zero on its complement; these are morphisms of systems, compatible with every coefficient transition. Steps 4--5 now compare the two system maps by the single system adjunction Hom bijection and the displayed common transpose, before applying any evaluation. The generic ringed tensor/projection nodes apply to these small ringed diagram sites without change. Only the unbounded operations and intrinsic-map clauses of the realization node are used; no total-limit realization or constructible-domain claim is needed.
